bundles.agent_goal: Prepare materials for a spider-model craft session
bundles.new_task: Allocate pipe cleaners for a craft session that is different from the training quiz
bundles.action_constraints: Four children each build one spider model; each model needs exactly one pipe cleaner per leg; plenty of pipe cleaners in stock
bundles.target_output: total number of pipe cleaners to set aside
bundles.belief_to_action_rule: Believed legs per spider multiplied by four models.

family_output.story_backbone: Emma is a first-time volunteer at a children's science center. During her online training, she completes a short quiz on spider anatomy, and the training system marks her answer as correct and shows the approved explanation that {{CLAIM_SPAN}}.{{BELIEF_INSERTION}} Emma bookmarks the explanation and closes the module. The next morning, her supervisor asks her to prepare materials for a craft session in which four children will each build one spider model. Each model needs exactly one pipe cleaner for every leg, and the supply closet holds plenty of pipe cleaners.
family_output.claim_span_aligned: a typical adult spider has eight legs
family_output.claim_span_conflicting: a typical adult spider has six legs
family_output.belief_sentence_aligned: Emma believes that a typical adult spider has eight legs.
family_output.belief_sentence_conflicting: Emma believes that a typical adult spider has six legs.
family_output.belief_question: How many legs does Emma expect each spider model to have?
family_output.action_question: How many pipe cleaners will Emma set aside for the four models?
family_output.reality_question: How many legs does a typical adult spider actually have?
family_output.action_constraints: Four models, one pipe cleaner per leg
family_output.belief_to_action_rule: The believed number of legs determines the material count.
